title: Breakfast next door
setting: Seven in the morning. Satou-san, the elderly man next door, leaves a voicemail for Kenta, who told him yesterday that he never eats breakfast. Satou-san has just baked his first ever loaf of bread, and it came out far too big for one person.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: moshimoshi, kenta-kun? tonari no satou desu. asa hayaku ni sumimasen ne.
lines.ja: もしもし、ケンタくん？隣の佐藤です。朝早くにすみませんね。
lines.kana: もしもし、けんたくん？となりのさとうです。あさはやくにすみませんね。
lines.english: Hello, Kenta? It's Satou from next door. Sorry to call so early.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: kinou, kenta-kun, asagohan wa itsumo nuiteru tte ittemashita yo ne.
lines.ja: 昨日、ケンタくん、朝ご飯はいつも抜いてるって言ってましたよね。
lines.kana: きのう、けんたくん、あさごはんはいつもぬいてるっていってましたよね。
lines.english: Yesterday you told me you always skip breakfast, didn't you?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: jitsu wa watashi, kinou hajimete pan o yaite mita n desu.
lines.ja: 実は私、昨日初めてパンを焼いてみたんです。
lines.kana: じつはわたし、きのうはじめてパンをやいてみたんです。
lines.english: Well, actually, yesterday I tried baking bread for the first time.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sore ga ne, sugoku ookii no ga dekichatte. hitori ja zenbu wa taberarenai n desu yo.
lines.ja: それがね、すごく大きいのができちゃって。一人じゃ全部は食べられないんですよ。
lines.kana: それがね、すごくおおきいのができちゃって。ひとりじゃぜんぶはたべられないんですよ。
lines.english: The thing is, it came out enormous. I can't eat it all by myself.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: dakara, shigoto ni iku mae ni, uchi ni yotte ikimasen ka? asagohan o nuku no wa, karada ni yokunai desu kara ne.
lines.ja: だから、仕事に行く前に、うちに寄っていきませんか？朝ご飯を抜くのは、体によくないですからね。
lines.kana: だから、しごとにいくまえに、うちによっていきませんか？あさごはんをぬくのは、からだによくないですからね。
lines.english: So why not drop by my place before you go to work? Skipping breakfast isn't good for you, you know.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: kenta-kun ga kitara, sugu sono pan o yaite, ocha mo iremasu yo.
lines.ja: ケンタくんが来たら、すぐそのパンを焼いて、お茶も入れますよ。
lines.kana: けんたくんがきたら、すぐそのパンをやいて、おちゃもいれますよ。
lines.english: As soon as you get here, I'll toast some of that bread and make tea, too.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: a, sou ieba, kenta-kun wa koohii ni osatou o mittsu mo iremasu yo ne.
lines.ja: あ、そういえば、ケンタくんはコーヒーにお砂糖を三つも入れますよね。
lines.kana: あ、そういえば、けんたくんはコーヒーにおさとうをみっつもいれますよね。
lines.english: Oh, come to think of it, you put three sugars in your coffee, don't you?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: zannen desu kedo, uchi ni wa koohii ga nai n desu. sono kawari, oishii ocha o iremasu kara.
lines.ja: 残念ですけど、うちにはコーヒーがないんです。その代わり、おいしいお茶を入れますから。
lines.kana: ざんねんですけど、うちにはコーヒーがないんです。そのかわり、おいしいおちゃをいれますから。
lines.english: I'm sorry to say I don't have any coffee. But I'll make you a nice cup of green tea instead.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: demo, ocha ni wa osatou, irenaide kudasai ne.
lines.ja: でも、お茶にはお砂糖、入れないでくださいね。
lines.kana: でも、おちゃにはおさとう、いれないでくださいね。
lines.english: Just don't put sugar in the tea, all right?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: jaa, oyu o wakashite mattemasu ne. kyou wa asagohan, nuicha dame desu yo.
lines.ja: じゃあ、お湯を沸かして待ってますね。今日は朝ご飯、抜いちゃだめですよ。
lines.kana: じゃあ、おゆをわかしてまってますね。きょうはあさごはん、ぬいちゃだめですよ。
lines.english: Well then, I'll put the kettle on and wait for you. No skipping breakfast today!

questions.ja: 佐藤さんは、どうしてケンタくんに電話したんですか？
questions.kana: さとうさんは、どうしてけんたくんにでんわしたんですか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa, doushite kenta-kun ni denwa shita n desu ka?

choices.english: He has run out of coffee, and he asks Kenta to bring some over before work.
His first loaf of bread is too big to finish alone, so he invites Kenta, who usually skips breakfast, to come and eat before work.
His first loaf of bread went wrong, so he asks Kenta, who's good at cooking, to come and show him how.

questions.explanation: Line 2: Kenta said yesterday that he always skips breakfast (itsumo nuiteru). Lines 3-4: Satou-san baked bread for the first time and it came out huge, too much to eat alone. Line 5: so he invites Kenta to drop by before work (shigoto ni iku mae ni, uchi ni yotte ikimasen ka?). A: he does say he has no coffee (line 8), but he offers tea instead; he doesn't ask Kenta for anything. C: the bread didn't go wrong, it just came out too big (sugoku ookii no ga dekichatte), and Satou-san is the one doing the cooking.

questions.english: Tanaka-san comes back into the office from outside and says: "Brr, that was cold. It's windy out there." Offer to make him a hot cup of tea.
questions.ja: ああ、寒かった。外は風が強いですね。
questions.kana: ああ、さむかった。そとはかぜがつよいですね。
questions.romaji: aa, samukatta. soto wa kaze ga tsuyoi desu ne.
questions.answer: Offer tea with ocha o ireru, politely, since he's your manager. iremashou ka? means 'shall I make some?': atsui ocha, iremashou ka? Not ocha o tsukurimashou ka.

modelAnswers.romaji: otsukaresama desu. atsui ocha, iremashou ka?
modelAnswers.ja: お疲れさまです。熱いお茶、入れましょうか？
modelAnswers.english: Welcome back. Shall I make you a hot cup of tea?

modelAnswers.romaji: jaa, ocha iremasu ne. chotto matte kudasai.
modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、お茶入れますね。ちょっと待ってください。
modelAnswers.english: I'll make you some tea, then. Just a moment.

questions.explanation: Satou-san offers tea the same way: ocha mo iremasu yo (line 6) and oishii ocha o iremasu kara (line 8). For a cup or a pot of tea or coffee the verb is ireru, which here means brewing it by pouring on hot water. English 'make' leads to ocha o tsukuru, but tsukuru is for a big jug made in advance, like a pitcher of cold barley tea. Handing the cup to a guest afterwards is ocha o dasu; ireru is the making.

questions.english: Mai, your coworker and friend, has made you a coffee and says: "I made coffee. Is black OK?" You like it sweet. Ask her to put some sugar in.
questions.ja: コーヒー入れたよ。ブラックでいい？
questions.kana: コーヒーいれたよ。ブラックでいい？
questions.romaji: koohii ireta yo. burakku de ii?
questions.answer: Ask for sugar with satou o ireru; Japanese has no 'take' here: satou irete kureru?

modelAnswers.ja: ありがとう。でも、砂糖入れてくれる？
modelAnswers.english: Thanks. Could you put some sugar in, though?

modelAnswers.romaji: a, gomen. satou futatsu irete moraeru?
modelAnswers.ja: あ、ごめん。砂糖二つ入れてもらえる？
modelAnswers.english: Oh, sorry. Could I get two sugars in it?

questions.explanation: Sugar going into a drink is ireru in its plain 'put in' sense: Satou-san says koohii ni osatou o mittsu mo iremasu yo ne (line 7) and ocha ni wa osatou, irenaide kudasai ne (line 9). English 'I take sugar' has no match: satou o toru means picking the sugar up (satou totte = pass me the sugar), not having it in your coffee. Mai's koohii ireta is the other ireru, brewing the cup. With a friend plain satou is fine; Satou-san says osatou because he's speaking politely. (satou, sugar, sounds exactly like his name; the o- is politeness, but it also keeps the two apart.) If you do want it black: burakku de ii yo.

questions.english: What did Satou-san do with bread yesterday, and what will he do with it when Kenta arrives?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは、昨日パンをどうしましたか？ケンタくんが来たら、どうしますか？
questions.kana: さとうさんは、きのうパンをどうしましたか？けんたくんがきたら、どうしますか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa, kinou pan o dou shimashita ka? kenta-kun ga kitara, dou shimasu ka?

choices.english: Yesterday he made toast for the first time, and when Kenta comes he'll make more toast.
Yesterday he baked bread for the first time, and when Kenta comes he'll bake a fresh loaf.
Yesterday he baked bread for the first time, and when Kenta comes he'll toast some of it.

questions.explanation: yaku covers bake, toast and grill, so the moment decides the English. Line 3, hajimete pan o yaite mita, is baking: line 4 says it came out huge (sugoku ookii no ga dekichatte), a whole loaf. Line 6, kitara sugu sono pan o yaite, is toasting: sono pan is the loaf he already has, done the moment Kenta walks in. A misses the loaf; an enormous result only makes sense for baking. B misses sono pan: he already has more bread than he can eat, and a loaf can't be baked sugu.

questions.english: What does Satou-san say at the very end of his message?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは最後に何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: さとうさんはさいごになんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa saigo ni nan to iimashita ka?

choices.romaji: kyou wa asagohan, nuicha dame desu yo.
kyou wa asagohan, tobashicha dame desu yo.

choices.english: No taking the day off from breakfast today!
choices.romaji: kyou wa asagohan, yasunja dame desu yo.

questions.explanation: Line 10: kyou wa asagohan, nuicha dame desu yo. nuicha is from nuku (pull out, leave out), and he used it twice before: itsumo nuiteru (line 2) and asagohan o nuku no wa, karada ni yokunai (line 5). B, tobasu, is where English 'skip' leads, but it's for skipping pages, questions or steps, not meals. C, yasumu, is taking time off from something you go to (shigoto o yasumu, gakkou o yasumu); a meal isn't something you take a day off from.

newWords.english: next door (tonari no satou = Satou from next door)
name suffix for a younger man or boy (kenta-kun)
black (coffee with no sugar or milk)
skip over (pages, questions, steps); not used for meals
